text:
sam.c: rolling alert — after today's rollout the kernel-routing tweak is producing memory pressure on longctx workloads. 3 dedicated pods OOM'd and restarted within 5m. seeing a lot of KV cache churn.
vivian: thanks. which commit? any CI failures pre-rollout?
sam.c: rollout was HEAD@a7b9c3 -> changed kernel selection policy to prefer low-latency kernels for seq>512. no CI perf red on basic perf-tests but 2 synthetic longctx suites weren't run.
chen.z: bisect looks like a7b9c3 is the culprit. reproduced locally with repro script: `scripts/repro_longctx_kv.sh --seq 2048 --clients 8` — OOM in 30s.
leo: profile dump from the repro attached: allocation heatmap shows repeated 32kb slab churn in kv_cache_allocator. HDR histogram of latencies shifted; p50 ok, p95/p99 spiked.
sam.c: deploying revert now? Can we patch kernel-routing to keep old path for seq>=1024? quick fix: `route_policy.set("force_large_kernels", true)`
vivian: quick bisect notes: a7b9c3 changed kernel selection to consult `historical_seq_profile` which caused more small-block kernels to be chosen for batched longctx because of batching heuristic edge-case.
ci-bot: perf-alert: longctx-suite-2 increased mem-peak by +48% at commit a7b9c3 (regression threshold 10%).
deploy-bot: auto-rollback triggered for rollout/2026-06-09 at 12:14 UTC.
chen.z: looking at kv cache eviction logs: eviction rate jumped x3, compaction runs overlap with allocation bursts -> fragmentation. suspect small-block kernels raise per-request temporary buffers that bypass kv cache prefix reuse.
leo: small snippet from perf tool:
``n# hot spots
kv_cache_allocator: 42% cpu
kernel_selection: 18% cpu
batcher: 12% cpu
```
sam.c: action items: 1) revert kernel-routing (done) 2) add targeted longctx perf tests in CI 3) add guard in routing to not switch kernels for longctx-heavy routes 4) postmortem if the revert didn't stabilize.
vivian: thanks — will follow-up with CI changes and a test matrix. tagging @sre for post-rollout watch.
deploy-bot: rollback completed. All impacted pods restarted and now stable.
sam.c: closing for now but leaving a7b9c3 on hold. we'll open a PR with a small-probe approach to kernel routing and add metrics to track kv churn.
